candidates.name: MUDAM
candidates.content: Designed by I.M. Pei of "Louvre Pyramid" fame, this museum showcases Luxembourgish artists and changing international exhibitions. The nonlinear (and rather confusing) building is half the fun, and on a quiet weekday afternoon in

candidates.name: The Bock
candidates.content: The rock on which the first castle stood, founded in 963 by Sigefroy (Sigfried). It is tied to a number of other remains of the old fortifications. Among others, the famous fortress builder Vauban built much in the city.

candidates.name: National Museum of History and Art
candidates.alt: French:fr|Musée national d'histoire et d'art, Luxembourgish: lu|Musée national um Fëschmaart, German: Nationalmuseum Geschichte and Kunst.
candidates.price: Free for permanent collections, but temporary exhibitions may have a cost
candidates.content: A very diverse museum, organized around the four departments of archaeology, coins and medals, decorative art, and fine art.

candidates.name: Grand Ducal Palace
candidates.content: Fully restored during the 1990s. It also houses the Luxembourgish Parliament the Chamber of Deputies. The palace is open for a period of 6 weeks over July and August whilst the Grand Duke and his family are away on their holidays.

candidates.name: Luxembourg City Museum
candidates.alt: Musée d'histoire de la Ville de Luxembourg
candidates.content: Museum about the history of the City of Luxembourg. The entire 1,000-year history is covered, though there is more emphasis on the social and economic history of the period after Luxembourg emerged as a fully independent state in

candidates.name: Notre Dame Cathedral
candidates.content: Built between 1613 and 1618 by Jesuits and was elevated to the status of cathedral in 1870. Nearby is the Gëlle Fra: literally 'Golden Lady'. This is a golden figure of a woman holding a wreath, a symbol of victory. It was taken d

candidates.name: Place Guillaume II
candidates.content: Place Guillaume II (also known in Luxembourgish as the "Knuedler") is the venue for a market every Wednesday and Saturday. It is also the site of an equestrian statue of William II of the Netherlands and Luxembourg and the neo-cla

candidates.name: National Museum of Natural History
candidates.content: Splendid expositions on minerals, animals, evolution, etc.

candidates.name: Musée Dräi Eechelen
candidates.content: Museum about the history of the Luxembourg Fortress inside an 18th century fort. Used to be free of charge, now 8€ entrance since 1/1/2026. Well worth a visit.

candidates.name: Tramways and Bus Museum
candidates.alt: Musée de tramways et de bus de la Ville de Luxembourg
candidates.content: The museum is next door to the AVL bus depot in Hollerich

candidates.name: Eglise St. Michel
candidates.content: This church took on its present form in 1688, but was probably built in the early 14th century. It was restored during 2003 and 2004.

candidates.name: Neumünster Abbey
candidates.content: Now a cultural and encounter centre with a nice church and the old St. John's hospital.

candidates.name: World War II Luxembourg American Cemetery and Memorial
candidates.hours: Open daily 09:00-17:00, except for Christmas and New Years Day.
candidates.content: In the eastern section of Luxembourg City, just south of the airport. The cemetery is the final resting place for 5,076 American military dead, most lost during the Battle of the Bulge. It is also the final resting place for Gener

candidates.name: Place d'Armes
candidates.content: In summer months the Place d'Armes is filled with tables and chairs from the surrounding cafes and at the centre of the square is the bandstand around which various concert seasons are based.

candidates.name: Grund
candidates.content: The Alzette, thought it is very small now, because the sandstone of the area is very soft, it dug out a huge valley. This is called the Ville Basse and is a spectacular area particularly the Grund (Statgrond) which is well worth t

candidates.name: The Kirchberg area
candidates.content: This area houses a number of banks and most of the European institutions in Luxembourg (Parliament, Court of Justice, Court of Auditors, European Investment Bank and some of the Commission's Directorate Generals). A number of buil

candidates.name: Am Tunnel
candidates.content: Art exhibitions inside a tunnel accessible through the headquarters of Luxembourg's savings bank.

candidates.name: Casino Luxemburg
candidates.content: Contemporary art forum with changing exhibitions.

candidates.name: Cemetery for German soldiers at Sandweiler
candidates.content: A World War II cemetery in Sandweiler, in southern Luxembourg. It contains the graves of 10,913 German servicemen from the Battle of the Bulge in winter 1944 and spring 1945. It is 1.5 km from the Luxembourg American Cemetery and

candidates.name: Bock Casemates
candidates.content: A network of underground fortifications, built in the 18th century. The fortifications and environs are recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

candidates.name: Le Chemin de la Corniche
candidates.content: Pedestrian promenade along the rim of the Alzette gorge, described as Europe's most beautiful balcony.

candidates.name: Pétrusse Casemates
candidates.content: Constructed by the Spanish in 17th century. They are not as large as the Bock Casemates.

candidates.name: Schueberfouer
candidates.content: Held every year in 2 weeks during end of August and early September, this huge funfair with roots dating back to the 14th century attracts enormous crowds. As well as the many stomach churning rides there are numerous places to ea

candidates.name: Philharmonie Luxembourg
candidates.content: Classical concerts.

candidates.name: Grand Théâtre de Luxembourg
candidates.content: Major venue for drama, opera and ballet.

candidates.name: Kinepolis Kirchberg
candidates.content: Largest multiplex cinema in the country, with restaurants and bars on the ground floor.

candidates.name: National Holiday
candidates.content: While not, despite its official name, the birthday of the current Grand Duke (or any preceding for that matter), June 23 is the country's national day. All-night street parties, fireworks and parades are enjoyed by seemingly the e

candidates.name: Chamber of Deputies
candidates.content: Those curious about the country's politics and hearing Luxembourgish spoken in a formal context can attend a public session of the Chamber of Deputies, Luxembourg's parliament. Check this page for the calendar of upcoming public s

candidates.name: LUXEXPO
candidates.content: Exhibition centre.

candidates.name: Swing Dance Luxembourg
candidates.content: Social dance on Mondays. During the summer it is outdoors in various locations; at other times it is at Scott’s Pub in Grund.

candidates.name: Decibel
candidates.content: A music bar in a courtyard alongside other bars and restaurants off the lively rue de Hollerich, an eclectic range of music can be heard here and Decibel has one of the widest range of Belgian beers in the city on tap and in bottl

candidates.name: The Black Stuff
candidates.content: The Black Stuff is an Irish pub on the outskirts of the city that is popular with ex-pats and locals alike. In the winter the log fire makes the cosy back room a good option to enjoy a Guinness or a hot port, the terrace is popula

candidates.name: Urban
candidates.content: A refreshingly modern bar that has a wide mix of clientèle. Although often overcrowded it is a great place to start a night out. Urban also has live music every Sunday evening and has sporting events shown on two massive plasma sc

candidates.name: The Tube
candidates.content: Subterranean, London Underground-themed bar. International young crowd and great tunes for various tastes. Gets extremely packed late on Fridays and Saturdays and overspills into the street during warmer months.

candidates.name: Britannia Pub
candidates.content: A favourite watering hole of local English ex-pats. Good place for watching football and rugby.

candidates.name: Pygmalion
candidates.content: Or the Pyg, an Irish pub and the best of the English, Scottish, Irish triumvirate in Clausen. Pub quizzes every other Monday.

candidates.name: Crossfire
candidates.content: A Scandinavian pub off Ave. de la Liberté, small and friendly.

candidates.name: Vis-a-vis
candidates.content: Hang out with the locals in this charming little Luxembourgish bar. Cheaper than a lot of other watering holes found in the city.

candidates.name: Café des Artistes
candidates.content: Smokey little Luxembourg piano bar illuminated by candlelight.

candidates.name: Melusina
candidates.content: Has a large main room with a balcony. It also has another couple of rooms at the back of the club which are worth a look.

candidates.name: Coco Mango
candidates.content: The bar of hotel Sofitel Grand Ducal enjoys some of the best views over the city. Pop in for a drink and enjoy!

candidates.name: Magnum
candidates.content: It's near the big parking lot (Glacis) just outside of the centre, but worth the walk there. No heels are too high and no skirts/shorts are too short here.

candidates.name: Scott's
candidates.content: No. 4, Bisserwee (down in the Grund). A common place for a drink (or two).

candidates.name: Café Interview
candidates.content: A real institution just off Place Émile-Hamilius, with a cozy, old-timey interior

candidates.name: KUMPIR The Happy Potato
candidates.content: The front counter lady is very kind and introduces you to all the dishes. Delicious baked potato with many kinds of toppings. During summer the tables outside are nice. They have other options if you don’t want to eat the potato.

candidates.name: Nirvana Café
candidates.content: The staff is so dedicated and kind. The dish of the day deal is excellent for vegan backpackers. The portion sizes are huge. The food is really tasty, Recommended is the chapati. Great lunch spot close to the train station. Delici

candidates.name: Brasserie Place "Russian Cafe"
candidates.content: Delicious food just like home. Some vegetarian options available. The service is very attentive. Always amazing quality food. Blini are hot and crispy, and pelmeni are tasty. Bortsch may be a bit oversavoury. Very local atmosphere

candidates.name: Café Santos Ribeiro
candidates.content: Canteen with Portuguese and a little international food. Lots of people from Luxembourg who like to eat well. Great place to eat lunch. Fast and delicious service. Family cooking. It feels like being in Portugal.

candidates.name: Snack Hakan
candidates.content: Clean and delicious mashamlah. The cheeseburger is very good. Best kebab. The owner is very customer oriented and very welcoming. Consistently good quality. The meat is tender and well seasoned. It's one of the best addresses for

candidates.name: Breaktime Kebab Grill - Gare
candidates.content: Very good kebab. Good options. Fresh and good ingredients. The boss and his employees are super friendly and courteous, it's always clean. The service is quite fast.

candidates.name: Mousel's Cantine
candidates.content: Great local plates on the site of the former Mousel brewery. Wash down huge portions of pork knee and broad beans with tankards of Mousel lager.

candidates.name: La Fontaine
candidates.content: One of a number of affordable bistros clustered around place de Paris. The quadrilingual menus run the gamut from pizza and mussels to Luxembourgish classics like judd mat gaardebounen (smoked pork neck with broad beans), and ther

candidates.name: Taj Mahal
candidates.content: By anyone's standards, a fantastic curry house serving rich and delicious Indian food. Very friendly staff too. Well worth making the short trip from the centre to this restaurant located near the station.

candidates.name: Restaurant Clairefontaine
candidates.content: This restaurant is at the foundation of exceptional dining. A pleasant gastronomic interlude in a magnificent setting. Creative dishes presented artfully by an exceptionally attentive staff. The quality of the lunch seduces you.

candidates.name: Les Jardins d'Anaïs
candidates.content: The beautiful environment, perfect service and delicious food makes it a truly spectacular experience. Your taste buds will thank you for a long time as the dishes you will taste are magical. Let yourself also be guided by the win

candidates.name: Glow - meal by meal
candidates.content: Delicious vegan food. Very popular so it's recommended to book a table. Space with indoor seating, and outdoor as well so you can soak up the sun.

candidates.name: Kirchberg Shopping Centre
candidates.content: A mixed-use complex, containing offices, a large shopping gallery anchored by a bi-level Auchan hypermarket, and a restaurant plaza.

candidates.name: Monthly Market in Glacis
candidates.content: Every month in the expansive Glacis square in Limpertsberg a market takes place, which is a mixture of a flea market, a farmer's market and some local arts & crafts. Browse and enjoy the best Luxembourg has to offer if you are in

candidates.name: lët’z go local
candidates.content: The organisation with the jocular name seeks to promote local Luxembourgish produce of all kinds, be it food, drinks, fashion, design or even leisure services. They organize markets multiple times every year in varying locations i

candidates.name: Weekly Market in Bonnevoie
candidates.content: Bonnevoie hosts a weekly market every Wednesday in front of the parish church

candidates.name: Market in Place de Paris
candidates.content: The Gare quarter holds markets in Place de Paris twice a week.
